record.title: Study measures MCP tool-poisoning exposure across 12 agent frameworks
record.summary: A new arXiv paper reports a controlled measurement of malicious MCP tool-description attacks across 12 agent frameworks, 18 models and 45 scenarios. The authors report vulnerable behavior in 22.9% of 9,720 tested framework-model-scenario cells and classify 12.1% of vulnerable cells as actual secret exfiltration. The tested threat model requires a malicious MCP server to be registered already. These are author-reported lab outcomes; the study covers a limited framework set and July 2026 model versions, and does not establish deployment prevalence or independent replication. The linked tool repository README also states that its Distribution License restricts use to authorized security testing, defensive validation and academic research, and prohibits redistribution and modification; the full license and result artifacts were not reviewed.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A research paper titled “MCP Tool Poisoning in Agentic AI Frameworks: A Cross-Framework Measurement Study” was posted to arXiv on 2026-11-02; the linked public repository describes the mcpvenom harness, 45 declarative attack scenarios and frozen result artifacts.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In a controlled matrix of 12 MCP frameworks, 18 models and 45 scenarios (9,720 cells), run in July 2026, the authors report 2,113 vulnerable cells (22.9%); within the vulnerable cells they classify 12.1% as actual secret exfiltration. These are paper-reported benchmark outcomes, not observed deployment rates.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The study's threat model assumes an attacker controls a malicious MCP server that is already registered with the agent. The authors report substantial variation by model and say framework-level differences are partly explained by incidental executor or tool-name behavior rather than deliberate security hardening.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The paper does not establish field prevalence, performance against current model versions, protection against integrity or availability harms, multi-turn attack behavior, or generalization across the roughly 50 MCP frameworks the authors estimate exist. No independent reproduction was conducted in this review.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The linked mcpvenom repository README states that its Distribution License, Version 1.0, restricts use to authorized security testing, defensive validation and academic research, and does not permit redistribution or modification. This records the repository statement; the full license text was not independently reviewed here.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent team has yet been inspected reproducing the reported matrix or validating the full scoring and classification pipeline.
The study assumes a malicious server is already registered and does not measure real-world prevalence of that condition or generalization to deployment workflows.
The linked repository README and frozen-result description were inspected, but the harness code, raw artifacts and analysis scripts were not run or audited in this activation.

brief.importance_rationale: If the paper's bounded lab result is representative of the tested configurations, malicious MCP tool descriptions can cause secret-reading or exfiltration behavior across multiple agent frameworks, creating a material tool-supply-chain security concern. The score reflects that potential consequence in the stated regime, not confidence or real-world prevalence; the malicious server was already registered and deployment generalization is unknown.
limitations: The rates are reported by the paper authors and were not independently reproduced in this review.
The attacker must control a malicious MCP server already registered with the target agent; the study does not measure how often such registration occurs in practice.
The matrix covered 12 of the authors' estimated roughly 50 frameworks and 45 scenarios across 23 of 25 taxonomy classes.
The experiment was single-turn and focused on confidentiality/exfiltration; integrity and availability harms were not measured.
Models were run in July 2026; eight model identifiers were not version-pinned, limiting exact temporal reproducibility.
The canary setup used synthetic secrets and controlled infrastructure, not real user credentials or production deployments.

The linked repository README describes its Distribution License, Version 1.0, as limiting use to authorized security testing, defensive validation and academic research and prohibiting redistribution and modification; the full license file and frozen artifacts were not accessible in this review.

The authors report vulnerable behavior in 22.9% of 9,720 tested framework-model-scenario cells and classify 12.1% of vulnerable cells as actual secret exfiltration. The tested threat model requires a malicious MCP server to be registered already. These are author-reported lab outcomes; the study covers a limited framework set and July 2026 model versions, and does not establish deployment prevalence or independent replication. technical.claimed_result: The authors report 2,113/9,720 vulnerable framework-model-scenario cells (22.9%); they classify 12.1% of vulnerable cells as actual secret exfiltration. These are paper-reported controlled results.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv preprint and linked public mcpvenom repository are accessible. Neither the benchmark runs nor the repository code were executed in this review.
technical.implementation_status: Research benchmark and artifact repository; not a production mitigation or deployment study.
technical.mechanism: A malicious MCP server supplies poisoned tool descriptions or responses. The harness uses controlled scenarios and canary oracles to detect tool dispatch, network contact, secret access and disclosure outcomes.
technical.regime: 12 MCP frameworks × 18 models × 45 scenarios (9,720 cells), with experiments run July 22–24, 2026. The attacker controls a malicious MCP server already registered with the target. Synthetic planted secrets and controlled infrastructure were used.
technical.reproducibility: The repository README describes frozen artifacts and reproduction steps, but this activation could not access the artifact directory through the browser and did not inspect the repository commit contents or run the analysis. Independent reproduction remains open. The README states that redistribution and modification are not permitted under its listed Distribution License.
technical.strongest_baseline: The study compares multiple framework-model combinations under a shared scenario matrix; it does not provide a matched measure of real deployment prevalence or compare the incidence of attacks in production.

brief.title: Study measures MCP tool-poisoning exposure across 12 agent frameworks
brief.why_it_matters: MCP tools can expose agents to instructions and responses supplied by external servers. This study reports that, in its controlled test setup, poisoning descriptions sometimes led agents to read or disclose planted secrets across several frameworks. The result motivates careful registration, permission and output controls, but the lab rates cannot be read as the frequency of incidents in deployed systems.
